title: Japanese Maple: Ancient Japanese Maples You Can Visit
meta_description: Usually a small shrub, rarely a monument. Two Dutch specimens made an official register; a Japanese temple maple has its autumn colour tracked every year.
intro: Japanese maples are usually shrubs, small enough to see over, so a specimen that clears a metre round and earns a place on an official monumental-tree register is genuinely unusual. The Netherlands has two on this site: one in Arnhem's Park Angerenstein, dated to the 1920s and protected on dendrological grounds alone, nothing historical attached, the tree itself being the whole reason; and one in Maastricht's Waldeckpark, whose register band of 1910 to 1920 sits oddly early against the park's own 1921 layout, a discrepancy nobody has resolved. Japan's own entry needs no register to prove itself: a temple maple in Iwaki whose age nobody will state, but whose autumn colour the city government tracks and publishes year by year, which is a different, more useful kind of record than an age nobody can verify.
